title: Luxor Eclipse Road Trip — Totality from the Roof of Hathor
intro: You said it yourself and then talked yourself out of it: it would be sweet to watch the eclipse from the roof of the Temple of Hathor. So that is where this trip goes. One road running south, every site on it and no doubling back — Meidum, then Tuna el-Gebel and the Thoth precinct at Hermopolis, then Beni Hasan, then Akhenaten's abandoned capital at Amarna, then Seti I at Abydos — and on 2 August the road ends on the roof at Dendera, at the head of the sixty miles of river you called the Band of Peace, above the best-preserved astronomical ceiling in Egypt, while the shadow crosses. Not Karnak. No viewing party, no crowd, nobody selling you a seat. You sleep outside Luxor throughout, so no eclipse-week room rate touches this, and Thebes comes afterwards — the royal tombs, then Karnak on your way to the night train, then Giza on the last day.

arrival.title: Arrival in Cairo — Wednesday 28 July
arrival.description:
Arrival at Cairo International Airport after a long first flight.
Our representative meets you airside and stays with you through the visa, passport and customs formalities, and collects your luggage with you — you are not left to work any of it out alone.
Private air-conditioned transfer to your hotel.
No sightseeing today, by your own request: Giza and the museum are held back to the very last day, once the eclipse crowds have gone home.
Dinner at the hotel and an early night. Tomorrow the road starts, and from here it only goes south.
Overnight in Cairo.
arrival.hotel: Cairo hotel, 3★ with pool (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: South to El-Minya — Meidum & the Thoth Precinct — Thursday 29 July
days.description:
Early breakfast and check-out; your Upper Egypt guide and driver are with you from here all the way south.
Meidum, the first stop on the road: Sneferu's pyramid began as a step pyramid and was cased into a true one, and the tower left standing is the core the collapsed casing exposed. You can go inside, down the descending passage to the corbelled chamber.
Then the ground you asked for by name. Tuna el-Gebel, the necropolis of Hermopolis: the tomb-chapel of Petosiris, built like a small temple and carved with Egyptian scenes in Greek dress, and the underground galleries where the sacred ibises and baboons of Djehuty were interred in their thousands.
Ashmunein, Hermopolis Magna itself — the cult centre of Thoth, where the two colossal baboons of Amenhotep III still stand over the ruins of his precinct. You wanted to see a temple of Djehuty; this is where his city was.
On to your hotel in El-Minya. Pool, dinner, early night.
days.hotel: El-Minya hotel, 3★ with pool (or equal) — half board

days.title: Beni Hasan & Tell el-Amarna — Friday 30 July
days.description:
Breakfast at the hotel, then Beni Hasan, a short way up the east bank.
The rock-cut tombs of the Middle Kingdom nomarchs, high in the cliff above the river: Khnumhotep II, Amenemhat and Baqet III, painted with wrestling holds, desert hunts, weaving and glass-making, and the caravan of Asiatics that scholars have argued over for a century. Almost no one comes here.
Then south to Tell el-Amarna — Akhetaten, the city Akhenaten raised on empty ground for a single god and abandoned within twenty years.
The boundary stelae, the North Palace, the Small Aten Temple on the open plain, and the royal tomb cut into the wadi behind the city, where the sun disc is carved with hands at the end of every ray.
You said the ancients taught you to give with both hands. Amarna is the one place they carved that idea into the rock, and you will have it very nearly to yourselves.
Back to El-Minya for the pool and dinner.
days.hotel: El-Minya hotel, 3★ with pool (or equal) — half board

days.title: On to Abydos — the Temple of Seti I — Saturday 31 July
days.description:
Breakfast and check-out, then the long leg south — roughly five hours before the stops, with comfort breaks as you need them and a packed breakfast box if you would rather sleep through the first hour.
Abydos in the afternoon, and the Temple of Seti I: the finest raised relief anywhere in Egypt, still holding its colour, the seven sanctuaries each with its own doorway, and the King List that names seventy-six of his predecessors in a single wall.
The Osireion behind the temple, sunk below the water table and built of blocks the size of the Giza casing stones.
You sleep at Abydos rather than pushing on, which keeps tomorrow short and unhurried — and tomorrow matters.
Dinner at the hotel. Overnight at Abydos.
days.hotel: Abydos / Sohag hotel, 3★ (or equal) — half board

days.title: Dendera — the Astronomical Ceiling, and the Roof — Sunday 1 August
days.description:
A slow breakfast and a short drive. Nothing today is rushed, on purpose.
Dendera, and your first visit to the Temple of Hathor — the whole thing, properly, with as long as you want and no clock. The astronomical ceiling cleaned of two thousand years of soot, the best-preserved painted ceiling in the country: the zodiac in the pronaos, Nut swallowing the sun at dusk and giving birth to it at dawn along the length of the hall, the crypts beneath the sanctuary, the Hathor-headed columns.
Then up the ascending staircase to the roof, where the New Year procession carried the goddess to meet the sun — the Osiris chapels, the open kiosk, and the view north over the Band of Peace.
We go up today deliberately, so that tomorrow you already know the ground, where the shade falls and where you want to stand.
Ten minutes on into Qena and your hotel for the next three nights — a working town, an ordinary hotel with a pool, food within walking distance, not one room priced for an eclipse.
Early supper, early night.
days.hotel: Qena hotel, 3★ with pool (or equal) — half board

days.title: Totality from the Roof of Hathor, Dendera — Monday 2 August
days.description:
An early start and the ten minutes back to Dendera, so that you are inside the enclosure and up on the roof long before anything begins.
This is the day the whole road was built for, and it is the thing you said you wanted and then assumed you could not have. The roof of the Temple of Hathor: your own space up there, shade rigged for you, cold water, certified solar viewing glasses, and your guide present for as much or as little as you want him.
Beneath your feet is the ceiling that maps this sky — the zodiac, the decans, the hours of the night — carved by people who spent their lives tracking exactly what is about to happen. Around you, the temple where the goddess was carried up to meet the sun each New Year.
The partial phases run for over an hour. The light goes wrong, the temperature drops, the birds stop. Then totality: this stretch of the Nile lies close to the point of greatest duration on this eclipse, one of the longest of the century. Exact local contact times are confirmed with you nearer the date.
Nobody selling seats, no viewing party, no crowd of strangers with cameras. Just the two of you, on the roof, at the head of the Band of Peace.
Back to Qena when you are ready — not before. Overnight in Qena.
days.hotel: Qena hotel, 3★ with pool (or equal) — half board

days.title: South to Thebes — the Royal Tombs & the West Bank — Tuesday 3 August
days.description:
Out early, an hour further south down the valley, and over to the west bank ahead of the heat.
The royal tombs: three on the standard ticket with your private Egyptologist, cut deep into the rock with their painted corridors and star-vaulted ceilings intact. Tutankhamun, Seti I and Nefertari are separately ticketed and can be added on the spot.
Deir el-Bahari, three colonnaded terraces built straight into the cliff at the head of the valley, with the Punt expedition reliefs along the middle colonnade.
Medinet Habu — the least visited and best preserved temple on the bank, colour still sitting in the migdol gate reliefs and the battle scenes running the length of the outer wall.
The two seated giants of Amenhotep III on the flood plain, all that survives above ground of a temple larger than the Amun precinct.
Back north out of the heat, to the pool and dinner. Overnight in Qena.
days.hotel: Qena hotel, 3★ with pool (or equal) — half board

days.title: The Amun Precinct, the Souk & the Night Train — Wednesday 4 August
days.description:
Check out after breakfast; your bags travel with you and you will not need a room tonight.
South one last time for the great precinct of Amun — quiet again now the eclipse has passed. The avenue of ram-headed sphinxes, the first pylon, the Great Hypostyle Hall and its hundred and thirty-four columns, the obelisks, the sacred lake, and the Botanical Chamber of Tuthmosis III with its carved catalogue of Syrian plants.
Then the Southern Sanctuary at the heart of the town, joined to the Amun precinct by the restored three-kilometre Avenue of Sphinxes, with the Roman and Islamic city built straight over the top of it.
The souk after that, for the shopping done properly: long-staple Egyptian cotton at a working cotton house rather than the tourist stalls, a scarf or head-wrap you can wear respectfully anywhere we take you, and a parasol, which is not a joke at this latitude in August with your colouring.
A light supper, then the station and the sleeper north — a private twin-berth cabin for the two of you, berths made up while you are at the window. You sleep the whole run and wake outside Giza.
days.hotel: Overnight sleeper train — private twin-berth cabin

departure.title: Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum & Departure — Thursday 5 August
departure.description:
Arrival at Giza in the early morning, met on the platform.
A day-use room at your hotel to shower, change and eat a proper breakfast before the day starts — nobody sightsees well straight off a train.
The Giza Plateau, privately: the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure, and the panoramic viewpoint where all three line up. Entry into the burial chamber is available on the spot at extra cost.
The Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple of Khafre. Sakkara can be swapped in for the museum if you would rather have the Step Pyramid — just say so.
The Grand Egyptian Museum: the hanging obelisk, the Ramses II atrium, the grand staircase of royal statuary, and the complete Tutankhamun collection, over five thousand objects with the death mask among them.
Time to eat and to buy anything you missed, then a private transfer to Cairo airport in good time, with final meet & assist through check-in. Safe journey home.

Meet & assist by our representative at Cairo International Airport on arrival and departure, and on the platform at both ends of the sleeper train
8 nights for two guests sharing one twin/double room — 1 night Cairo, 2 nights El-Minya, 1 night Abydos, 3 nights Qena, 1 night in a private sleeper cabin
No night in Luxor at any point, deliberately: you never pay an eclipse-week room rate, and Thebes is seen by day from a base an hour north
Two visits to Dendera — the full temple and the roof on 1 August, and the roof again on eclipse day, with entrance fees for both
Roof access at the Temple of Hathor on 2 August arranged under special permit, with shade, seating, cold water and certified solar viewing glasses for both guests
3★ hotels chosen for a pool and food within walking distance — half board everywhere south of Cairo, bed & breakfast in Cairo
Day-use room in Cairo on 5 August to shower and rest between the night train and your flight home
Overnight sleeper train Luxor – Cairo in a private twin-berth cabin, with supper and breakfast served on board
Private air-conditioned vehicle with driver for the whole road trip, at your disposal alone — never shared, no group at any point
Two separate guide and driver teams: one for the road south and Upper Egypt, one for Cairo and Giza
All meals and accommodation for your driver and guide are our cost, not yours — you are not asked to feed anybody
Private licensed Egyptologist guide on every sightseeing day, with no fixed clock at Dendera, Amarna or the Thoth precinct
Entrance fees to every site named in the programme, including three tombs in the Theban necropolis, Beni Hasan, Amarna, Abydos, Karnak and the Southern Sanctuary
Guided visit to a working Egyptian cotton house for clothing, a scarf or head-wrap, and a parasol — no obligation to buy anything
Dinner on arrival night, and a light supper before you board the night train
Bottled water in the vehicle throughout, and cold water on the temple roof on eclipse day
All local taxes and service charges
24/7 contact with our Cairo office for the whole nine days, in your time zone as well as ours
Written booking confirmation setting out the payment schedule and cancellation terms in full before any deposit is taken
excluded:
International airfare to and from Egypt — book this now; eclipse-week seats will go early
Egypt entry visa (USD 36, payable on arrival)
Any special eclipse-day permit fee or surcharge set by the Ministry of Tourism & Antiquities for roof access at Dendera — not published at the time of quoting. This is the one figure here that can move, and we confirm it in writing as soon as it is known; if the permit is refused we substitute a private terrace at Qena and refund the difference
Lunches throughout — left out deliberately to hold the price down; your guide will take you to good, cheap local places, or we can add them on request
Optional entry inside the Great Pyramid at Giza, and the separately ticketed tombs of Tutankhamun, Seti I and Nefertari — all payable on the spot
Optional sunrise hot-air balloon over the Theban west bank — quoted on request, and it would mean an overnight in Luxor
Anything you buy at the cotton house or in the souk
Drinks with meals and anything from the hotel bar
Travel insurance — strongly recommended for a trip booked this far ahead
Tipping and gratuities for the guide and driver
Personal expenses, laundry and telephone calls
